chunks: Ali, from Ali ibn Shiyrah, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Husayn al-Harshoush, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The people are speaking against us and refuting our statement that Salat (funeral prayer) is not prayed over a child because he has not prayed (Salat). They say: Salat is not prayed except over one who has prayed. So we say: Yes. They say: What is your view if a Christian or a Jew were to become Muslim, then died immediately, what is the answer regarding him?' He said: 'Say to them: What is your view if this one who became Muslim immediately then forged a lie against a person, what would be obligated upon him regarding his forgery?' If they say: 'The Hadd (legal punishment) is obligated upon him,' then it is said to them: 'So if this child who has not prayed were to forge a lie against a person, would the Hadd be obligated upon him?' If they say: 'No,' then it is said to them: 'You are correct. Salat is only prayed over one upon whom Salat and the Hadds are obligated, and Salat is not prayed over one upon whom neither Salat nor the Hadds are obligated.'
ai.seo_question: Why is funeral prayer not prayed over children according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the claim that funeral prayer is exclusive to those who performed daily Salah by employing a precise legal analogy with *Hudud* (fixed punishments). He demonstrates that just as a child is exempt from the penalty of *Qadhf* (false accusation) due to lack of full legal responsibility (*taklif*), they are similarly exempt from the obligation of Salah, thereby establishing that the prerequisite for funeral prayer is the obligation of the prayer itself, not its actual performance. This reasoning underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that *Salat al-Janazah* is a consequence of the deceased's duty to pray, rather than a reward for having prayed.

en.hubeali: Ali, from Ali Bin Saheyra, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from Husayn Al Harshous, from Hisham Bin Salim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The people are speaking against us and are refuting our words that Salaat is not to be prayed upon the childen because they did no pray Salaat, except upon the ones who did pray Salaat. So we are saying, Yes’. So they are saying, ‘What is your view if a Christian or a Jewish man were to become a Muslim, then dies at that time, what would be the answer with regards to it?’ So heasws said: ‘Say to them, ‘What is your view if this one who did become a Muslim, then at that time were to forge a lie against a person, what (Punishment) would be Obligated upon him regarding his forgery?’ So if they would be saying, ‘The legal Punishment (Hadd) would be Obligated upon him’. So if they do say this, say to them, ‘So if this child who did not pray Salaat were to forge a lie against a person, would the legal Punishment (Hadd) be Obligation upon him?’ So if they are saying, ‘No’, then it would be said to them, ‘You are speaking the truth. But rather, it is Obligated for him to be prayed Salaat upon the one whom the Salaat and the legal Punishments were Obligated upon, and he would not be prayed Salaat upon, the one whom neither the Salaat nor the legal Punishments (Hadds) were Obligated upon’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali has narrated from Ali ibn Shirah from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from Husayn al-Harshush from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that people speak against us and do not accept our words, ‘there is no Salah (prayer) for a deceased child’; he has not performed any Salah (prayer). They say, ‘You say that there is no Salah (prayer) for those who have not performed any Salah (prayer).’ We say, ‘Yes that is true.’ They say, ‘Consider if a Christian or a Jew becomes a Muslim, then he dies within the same hour, then what is the answer?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Ask them to consider the case of this man, new Muslim, if he within the same hour falsely accuses a human being. What is his obligation because of his committing such sin? They will say that he is subject to punishment according to law. When they say this, then it is said to them, ‘If a child who has not performed any Salah (prayer) accuses a human being falsely, is he subjected to punishment according to law? They will say that he is not subject to any punishment. It then is said to them that you are right. Salah (prayer) is necessary for one who has performed Salah (prayer) and those who are subject to punishment according to law. Salah (prayer) is not necessary for one on whom Salah (prayer) is not obligatory or enduring punishment according to law.’”
